extracted.intended_audience: small business applicants preparing NIAID SBIR (NIAID-AT-SBIR R43/R44) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling a complete NIAID SBIR (R43/R44) grant application using the SF424 (R&R) / PHS 398 format; includes required attachments (project summary, public health relevance, facilities, vertebrate animals, biosketches, budgets, commercialization plan, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity's instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format. Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the current FOA and agency-specific instructions; sample applications are illustrative only and may be out of date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and permitted use of posted application text
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the application is copyrighted. The awardee provided express permission for NIAID to post this grant application and summary statement for educational purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use the material (e.g., data, writing, graphics) for nonprofit educational purposes only, provided the material remains unchanged and the principal investigators, awardee organizations, and NIH NIAID are credited.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA confidentiality and redactions
rubrics_metrics.description: When NIH responds to FOIA requests for grant applications and summary statements, the material will be subject to FOIA exemptions and include substantial redactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH must protect all confidential commercial or financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 conformance and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Note on Section 508 Conformance and Accessibility. We have reformatted this sample to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have trouble accessing the content, contact the NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources at deaweb@niaid.nih.gov. Ensure your application materials conform to accessibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF424 (R&R) required fields and applicant certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The SF 424 (R&R) face page and applicant information must include: Type of submission, Applicant organizational DUNS, Legal name, Employer Identification (EIN/TIN), Type of applicant, Descriptive project title, Proposed project start and end dates, Congressional district, PD/PI contact information, and Estimated project funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By signing the application the authorized representative certifies the statements and agrees to required assurances; false statements may subject signatory to criminal/civil penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). Ensure accuracy and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents / Required application components
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must include specific components and attachments such as: SF424 R&R Face Page; Project Summary/Abstract; Public Health Relevance Statement; Facilities & Other Resources; Other Attachments; Biographical Sketches for Senior/Key Persons; Research & Related Budgets (Years 1–4) and Budget Justification; SBIR/STTR Information including Commercialization Plan and Prior SBIR Phase II Awards; PHS 398 Specific Cover Page Supplement; PHS 398 Specific Research Plan sections (Introduction, Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Vertebrate Animals, Bibliography & References Cited, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plan); PHS 398 Checklist; Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide page numbers and include all listed attachments. Follow specified order and include required SBIR-specific documents (e.g., commercialization plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary / Abstract content
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise description of project goals, significance, rationale and planned approach (example: goal to develop a therapeutic capable of sterilizing recalcitrant chronic infections, rationale for choice of mechanism, key preclinical models to be used, and intended next steps toward IND/clinical trials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize significance, innovation, approach and expected outcomes in a way that reviewers can quickly assess importance and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance Statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A plain-language statement describing the public health relevance of the project (example summary: 'The goal of the project is to develop a therapeutic capable of curing currently untreatable chronic infections...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain in nontechnical terms why the work matters to public health; this is a required attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects and Vertebrate Animals reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research & Related Other Project Information must indicate whether human subjects or vertebrate animals are involved, whether the project is exempt, and provide IRB/IACUC approval dates and assurance numbers as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects: indicate exemption status and IRB details. If vertebrate animals: provide IACUC approval date and Animal Welfare Assurance number; do not proceed without appropriate approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit description of laboratory space, equipment, adjacent common facilities, access to institutional core facilities, animal facilities, computers and software, and biohazards containment and programs (example: description of Arietis lab space, list of instruments, and core facilities access at BU Medical Center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the environment is adequate to accomplish the work, list specific instrumentation and institutional resources, and describe institutional animal and safety support (accreditation, oversight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal facilities and AAALAC accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: If animal studies will be performed, identify the animal care facility (example: Laboratory Animal Science Center at Boston University) and state accreditation (AAALAC) and scope of animal housing/support spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe staffing, veterinary oversight, SOPs, training, recordkeeping, and administrative support to show appropriate animal care infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and biohazards compliance (BSL-level, training, procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: State biosafety level for pathogens (example: S. aureus is BSL-2), laboratory certification (BSL-2 certified), and that all personnel receive annual BSL-2 and other safety training; describe PPE, sterilization, spill response, and institutional biosafety committee (IBC) review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document training, certification, waste handling procedures (e.g., 10% bleach treatment, autoclaving), annual equipment certification (biological safety cabinets), strain logging, and occupational health monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals — euthanasia methods and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe euthanasia methods to be used and state whether consistent with AVMA Panel on Euthanasia recommendations (example: CO2 inhalation with secondary cervical dislocation; methods consistent with AVMA and institutional policies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state chosen method(s), justify selection, and affirm consistency with AVMA and institutional welfare policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals — monitoring and humane endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe animal observation frequency and humane endpoints (example criteria: refusal of food/water, clinical dehydration, prolonged decreased food intake, muscle atrophy/lethargy, decreased body condition score of 2.5 or less on 1–5 scale; animals observed at least once daily; euthanize moribund or if next observation >12 hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify how often animals will be checked, measurable clinical endpoints, and clear euthanasia triggers to minimize suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR small business registration and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide SBIR.gov SBC registration control ID and company information (company name, address, TIN/EIN, DUNS, company URL, number of employees, percent ownership by venture capital/hedge funds/private equity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accurate SBC registration and answer ownership/size questions required for SBIR eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical Sketch: Provide required information for Senior/key personnel following the prescribed format. DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Name, eRA Commons user name, Position Title, Education/Training (institution, degree, MM/YY, field), and sections A–D: A. Personal Statement; B. Positions and Honors; C. Selected Peer-reviewed Publications; D. Research Support (ongoing/completed in past 3 years). Follow the order and content headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key Personnel attachments — biosketch and current & pending support
rubrics_metrics.description: For each listed Senior/Key Person attach Biographical Sketch and Current & Pending Support documents; indicate project role and other project role category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach PDFs for each person and label clearly; ensure roles (PD/PI, consultant, etc.) are specified and current & pending support is disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support content
rubrics_metrics.description: Include letters from consultants/collaborators describing commitments and relevant expertise (examples provided from collaborators describing consultation on PK/PD, hollow-fiber studies, and ongoing collaboration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should state the nature of collaboration, services to be provided, and evidence of expertise to strengthen the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a plan to disseminate results (example: publish in professional journals such as Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy and present at meetings such as ICAAC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State intended dissemination routes and any data/material sharing strategies as required by NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Checklist and required certifications/disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the PHS 398 Checklist including application type, change of investigator/institution questions, inventions and patents disclosure (for renewals), program income, and a disclosure permission statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer checklist questions accurately and provide program income estimates and disclosure permissions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget documents and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Research & Related Budget pages for each budget year (Years 1–4), Cumulative Budget, and a Budget Justification attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed cost breakdowns and narrative justification for personnel, supplies, animals, cores, and other costs in line with FOA budget instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR-specific attachments: Commercialization Plan and prior SBIR awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach an SBIR Commercialization Plan and list Prior SBIR Phase II Awards where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe market opportunity, commercialization strategy, milestones, and prior SBIR history; attach required supporting documents.
